frog.speaker: H
frog.excerpt: We left Bamiyan and drove to the red city.  We went 5km farther to some springs.  There were some hot and cold springs.  There was a very big river between some high rocky mountains.  Several times the river disappeared in to the rocks.  One pool, big enough to swim in, had concrete sides.  There were 2 very forcing hot springs in the pool which would push a stick up if you threw it in.  F and I found a toad (well I think it was a toad), it surprised us by hopping up the dry mountain.  After lunch we went to the red city.  We bought some tourmaline.

fred.speaker: D
fred.excerpt: In the morning, after getting some money, we drove off to Herat.  Fred stopped, and our bicycling friend came up, he and Dad fiddled a bit and then Fred started again.  We drove into Herat, it was a dirt track in between mud(?) houses, we stopped to buy the first bread in Afghanistan, and some fruit.  We drove past lots of small shops and out onto a big square, we went onto a tarmac road, and started looking for a campsite.  We stopped in a park for lunch, and then went to look for the bazaar, resolving to find a campsite afterwards.  We never actually found the bazaar but the people were interesting.

fred.speaker: F
fred.excerpt: We got some money and set off to Herat. We passed an English bicyclist, who had had coffee with us last night. He had been through Africa, Greece, Turkey and Iran, and was just starting on Afghanistan. We gave him a Change of Address card. We went on a bit when Fred broke down, so we had a coffee, then the man on the bike came, so dad and him had a go on the engine. They fixed it and we went to Herat.

fred.speaker: D
fred.excerpt: We found a Hotel, called the ‘Salang Hotel’ and we camped in it’s garden, they had an enormous pelican and two ducks.  In the morning we all had hot showers, the water was heated by an old boiler, and we had to keep wood in it.  In the morning we washed clothes, and tidied Fred, then Mum & Dad rushed off to the bank, only to find that it is closed at 12.00, not 1.00.  We had lunch and then went out, taking our old radio with us.  We walked up the main street, there were lots of fur and leather shops there, I tried on some sheepskin jackets, but they had been very badly cured, and they were smelly.

fred.speaker: D
fred.excerpt: We drove Fred up, and had lunch overlooking a beautiful lake, it rained a bit, so we packed up and started, earlier than we had been expected.  The road was wet and slippery, and it had been snowing again.  We came to one hill and it was all clay, so the wheels were spinning.  Mum and I got out to push, while F & H bounced inside to try and get the wheels to grip.  Mum and I got out two mats, we put them under the back wheels, and pushed some more, at last we got onto some stonier ground and Fred got moving by himself.  Mum and I were very muddy, and it started snowing again.  Dad drove quite a way to get out of the danger spot, so Mum and I had to walk a long way.  When we got there, Dad was putting some petrol from the jerry can into Fred, as we were using up a lot of it.  We drove on quite a way but the road was getting very wet and slushy; at last we felt the wheels spinning again. Mum and I jumped out, and started pushing, but to no avail.  The sky was very cloudy, but ther sun seemed to be shining over the lakes (grunt, growl).  We got the carpets out again, but the road was so wet, that they got just as slippery.  And the tyres spun so much on them, that they burnt.  We fixed ropes on the front and tried pulling, then Dad came and tried, I was freezing, ‘specially my fingers and toes.  After almost an hour we gave up, we had tried everything, we moved about 3m, and then nothing would budge us, except for creeping forward, an inch or so.

fred.speaker: D
fred.excerpt: We got back in Fred, I just couldn’t warm up.  F made us some coffee.  We hoped that someone would come and tow, or push us, but no one did, we were thinking that we would have to spend the night there, when we heard the faint sound of an engine.  I thought perhaps that it was our imagination playing tricks, but soon a little Russian bus came into sight.  They needed some oil, so Dad got ours out, and while the man was fiddling with the engine, the other people helped push, with 6 strong people pushing, we only just got going.

fred.speaker: H
fred.excerpt: We are bogged in a snowy mountain.  We have been trying to get Fred up a muddy hill, wet with melted snow.

fred.speaker: D
fred.excerpt: Mum & Dad got the oil that we had lent to the bus back, we were still in bed when they went to get it.  After breakfast, we went to the local pump, we filled up the tank and did the washing up, the water was lovely and clean, it came straight up from a spring.  We left Bamiyan, drove to the ‘Red City’, we had lunch at some warm springs, they were a lovely temperature.  At the Red City, there were some little boys, they had some pretty crystals, some were tourmaline, they were all from the surrounding mountains.  We bought one, for 2 Afs, then parked Fred and started climbing, leaving Mum in the car.  There was a nice guard, he helped the children climbing off the paths instead of calling them down.  Some of the towers had beautiful brickwork.  It was tiring climbing.

fred.speaker: F
fred.excerpt: We left Bamiyan to go to the Red City. On the turnoff next to a hotel we asked whether it was the right road; they told us it was and that it led to some hot springs. We decided to go to the hot springs first, because they were furthest away.  We were driving along when Dad heard the noise of water, but we couldn’t see it, so we got out and had a look. H and I went ahead and found the spring. Soon after, the others came in Fred. We had lunch and visited the Red City the rest …

fred.speaker: H
fred.excerpt: When we woke up there was ice inside Fred.  We drove along a river in a gorge and stopped for lunch by the river which had become very muddy.  After lunch, D, F and I started digging a cave community in a cliff.  While we were digging some camels came, among them were two very small ones.

puncture_tyre_breakdown.speaker: F
puncture_tyre_breakdown.excerpt: We left Herat and went along semi-desert. Then turned onto a grit road. It was very dusty; everything got covered with dust. There were lots of nomads and camels with big flocks. We forded a river or two. They had concrete so that we would not bog down. The water made a nice noise on the tyres. Then we drove to some ruins; they used to be a summer palace. Then we went on a bit to the restored arch of Bost. It was near a fortified hill and within the fort’s walls up on the hill there were lots of big walls (as well as those on the ground).The hill had a deep hole with lots of rooms on either side [pic]. Someone said they were dungeons. We went in. Two people followed us. There were lots of little hard squiggly black things, like this [pic]. They ponged like nothing on earth. We thought the holes were not dungeons but places where people lived. Some were dark. In one place the tunnel was dark and on a slope with only rubble and lots of sand-dust. We kept on falling and choking in the dust we kicked up.

puncture_tyre_breakdown.speaker: F
puncture_tyre_breakdown.excerpt: When we forded the big river there was a small foot suspension bridge [pic]. It swayed in the wind. The water was very clear. A boy was fishing from the bridge. The water made a nice noise against the tyres.  On the way back from the ruins to the non-grit road we had a blow-out. There was a big hole in the tyre.

puncture_tyre_breakdown.speaker: D
puncture_tyre_breakdown.excerpt: We drove on and on, on a dirt track, until we had a blow out, it was one of the new tyres, we changed it and then drove on, until at last we got onto the smooth main road.  After an hours or two’s driving, we entered Kandahar.  We bought some bread, and then drove off to a park for lunch, that Fodor mentions, it was miles away, over a small mountain pass, when we got there it was nice though.  After lunch, we drove back into Kandahar to see the throne of ‘Babul’ (first of the great Moguls), it had 42 steps leading up to it (puff, pant).  We found a Bakerie, selling doughnuts, and apple pies, and other delicious things, it also sold Hard cheese, we spent just under £2.00 there - man - delicious!  We stayed in a campsite.  H & I had a lovely hot shower.  We had cauliflower cheese for dinner.

puncture_tyre_breakdown.speaker: D
puncture_tyre_breakdown.excerpt: We met a man called Colin in a Landrover, a girl called Miranda was travelling with him from Tehran.  We went into town, Dad went to the Tyre shop, but it was closed, so Mum drove back to the Hotel to ask the tyre-man’s brother (who owned the Hotel) what was happening.  Dad waited by the tyre shop, and F, H & I went to the ‘Baksheesh Bakerie’ again, we spent 18 Afs, between us.  We got back to Dad, and soon the tyre man came, with the tyre, mended.  From the shop, we phoned Mum, she has having trouble with the car, so we hailed a Taxi (tiny 3 wheeled approx 5 seater) and us 4 plus a mechanic, the driver and a tyre squeezed in and drove to the Hotel.  While everyone fiddled with the car, F, H & I had eggs and chips in the restaurant, delicious chips.

puncture_tyre_breakdown.speaker: F
puncture_tyre_breakdown.excerpt: We went to get the tyre but the shop was closed, so us children went to a bakery and bought some food to munch while we waited for the tyre to be vulcanised. When we got it we went into a taxi and drove to Kandahar.

puncture_tyre_breakdown.speaker: H
puncture_tyre_breakdown.excerpt: We were in the Aria Hotel.  Denise, Daddy, Francis and I went to town and all us children went to the bakshish bakery.  We bought several things and then went back to the tyre shop where Daddy was waiting for it to open.  Quite soon it opened.  We went back to the Hotel in a bubble taxi, 5 of us, a tyre and the driver.  The bubble taxi had three wheels.  I had to sit on Denise’s lap.  We had egg and chips for lunch in the hotel restaurant and told a ghost story which we called the Curse of the Green Hands.

puncture_tyre_breakdown.speaker: D
puncture_tyre_breakdown.excerpt: We drove Fred up, and had lunch overlooking a beautiful lake, it rained a bit, so we packed up and started, earlier than we had been expected.  The road was wet and slippery, and it had been snowing again.  We came to one hill and it was all clay, so the wheels were spinning.  Mum and I got out to push, while F & H bounced inside to try and get the wheels to grip.  Mum and I got out two mats, we put them under the back wheels, and pushed some more, at last we got onto some stonier ground and Fred got moving by himself.  Mum and I were very muddy, and it started snowing again.  Dad drove quite a way to get out of the danger spot, so Mum and I had to walk a long way.  When we got there, Dad was putting some petrol from the jerry can into Fred, as we were using up a lot of it.  We drove on quite a way but the road was getting very wet and slushy; at last we felt the wheels spinning again. Mum and I jumped out, and started pushing, but to no avail.  The sky was very cloudy, but ther sun seemed to be shining over the lakes (grunt, growl).  We got the carpets out again, but the road was so wet, that they got just as slippery. After almost an hour we gave up, we had tried everything, we moved about 3m, and then nothing would budge us, except for creeping forward, an inch or so.

camel.speaker: H
camel.excerpt: We got some money from ye bank.  We started to go to Herat.  We saw the bicyclist and broke down.  When we were going again we saw some camels then Mum and Dad and Denise went and visited some windmills.  When we reached Herat and had a look around a bazaar we went to a Hotel see ??? at ???

camel.speaker: D
camel.excerpt: We went and had lunch in a park, just out of town, we were just about to drive out, when Dad remembered the blue glass beads that we saw, so, back we went!  We bought 3 strings of beads.  And then at last, we got on the road to Kandahar.  We drove through lots of scrub/desert and small mountains, there were lots of Nomad tents and camels.  At last we found a place to camp, it was near a dried up river bed, in the bank, F, H & I dug some caves, for the Villas, Hills, Oppies and Us, the bank was about two feet higher than me.

camel.speaker: D
camel.excerpt: We’ve seen lots and lots of camels and nomads etc - it was difficult to find a spot to camp, free from them.  We saw the beginnings of sand dunes.  We also saw some big mirages of lakes and things.  We turned a corner, and the ground was covered by pink flowers, they were small, dry pink bubbles on spikey little plants, we drove on a bit, and then there were none.  Beautiful sunset.

camel.speaker: F
camel.excerpt: We left Herat and went along semi-desert. Then turned onto a grit road. It was very dusty; everything got covered with dust. There were lots of nomads and camels with big flocks. We forded a river or two. They had concrete so that we would not bog down. The water made a nice noise on the tyres. Then we drove to some ruins; they used to be a summer palace. Then we went on a bit to the restored arch of Bost. It was near a fortified hill and within the fort’s walls up on the hill there were lots of big walls (as well as those on the ground).The hill had a deep hole with lots of rooms on either side [pic]. Someone said they were dungeons. We went in. Two people followed us. There were lots of little hard squiggly black things, like this [pic]. They ponged like nothing on earth. We thought the holes were not dungeons but places where people lived. Some were dark. In one place the tunnel was dark and on a slope with only rubble and lots of sand-dust. We kept on falling and choking in the dust we kicked up.

camel.speaker: F
camel.excerpt: Helena and I went to look at a camel. He had a blanket with a hole in it. The hole was for his hump. (pic)

camel.speaker: D
camel.excerpt: We drove through some eerier, but very beautiful gorges until we came to Doab, there, we wanted to turn off to see the beautiful ‘Valley of Kings’ but the way was barred.  We found a Policeman, he took us to a house.  Upstairs was an old telephone and ??  ?? he found out that it would cost 10 dollars each, so we left it.  At lunch we dug caves and saw lots of camels.

camel.speaker: H
camel.excerpt: When we woke up there was ice inside Fred.  We drove along a river in a gorge and stopped for lunch by the river which had become very muddy.  After lunch, D, F and I started digging a cave community in a cliff.  While we were digging some camels came, among them were two very small ones.

camel.speaker: D
camel.excerpt: When we woke up, we were surrounded by camels.  We counted at least 70, but they were very spread out, and there were quite a few which we couldn’t see.  We could only see one man looking after them, someone later told us that they could be worth 10,000 Afs (£140).  That meant that the flock could have been worth about 700,000 Afs (£?!)

camel.speaker: F
camel.excerpt: In the morning, camel after camel slowly and casually sauntered past. They were black or brown or white or mixtures. Dad counted at least 70 camels, but there was only one man. A camel is worth about £140.

camel.speaker: H
camel.excerpt: We woke up on Friday morning and found that we were surrounded by a herd of 70 or more camels, who seemed to be herded by only one man.  We left quite early to drive to Mazar-i-Sharif to see the buzkashi, which is a game played on horseback with a dead goat or calf as ball.  Unfortunately the buzkashi was not on as the teams were away in Kabul.  We met a Pathan(?) [Pashtun] from the Khyber Pass, he had come to buy eagles.  He had bought two and was sending them to Saudi Arabia, they were worth 15,000 AF each!

bazaar.speaker: D
bazaar.excerpt: In the morning, after getting some money, we drove off to Herat.  Fred stopped, and our bicycling friend came up, he and Dad fiddled a bit and then Fred started again.  We drove into Herat, it was a dirt track in between mud(?) houses, we stopped to buy the first bread in Afghanistan, and some fruit.  We drove past lots of small shops and out onto a big square, we went onto a tarmac road, and started looking for a campsite.  We stopped in a park for lunch, and then went to look for the bazaar, resolving to find a campsite afterwards.  We never actually found the bazaar but the people were interesting.

bazaar.speaker: H
bazaar.excerpt: We got some money from ye bank.  We started to go to Herat.  We saw the bicyclist and broke down.  When we were going again we saw some camels then Mum and Dad and Denise went and visited some windmills.  When we reached Herat and had a look around a bazaar we went to a Hotel see ??? at ???

bazaar.speaker: H
bazaar.excerpt: By the time we left the man had not arrived with Francis’ turban and cap and when we drove through the bazaar we looked for him but did not see him.  After that we drove and drove and drove not even stopping for lunch which was bread and dates and grapes.  When we got to Ghazni, we saw lots of ruins and then went to the museum.  At the museum there was a carving of an elephant - like this (Pic).

bazaar.speaker: D
bazaar.excerpt: We then drove onto Landi Kotal.  Dad, F & I went down to see the bazaar, which was supposed to have a big black market.  Dad asked if there was any alcohol, and a man said ‘No, but Hasheesh, Morphine and Cocain, in my shop’.  We drove on and came to Peshawar, at length we found ‘Deans Hotel’ we stayed there.  H & I had a lovely long bath.

mosque.speaker: H
mosque.excerpt: The shop was very interesting.  Herat has no tarmac roads but lots of horse and carriages.  The horses have lots of red bomboms on then and some had bells.  There are lots of hotels as well.  Herat has a Friday Mosque.  There are lots of weavers who weave silk on looms.  The looms are in rooms side by side that you can see into.  All the looms had horse hair on them.  Men wove using both hand and foot.  The silk was bright patterns.

mosque.speaker: D
mosque.excerpt: When we woke up, Francis and I went to get the bread, I wore my chouda.  After breakfast, we went to visit the Friday Mosque, we went in, and up a corridor, til we came to a big courtyard, we took off our shows, then a policeman came and said we could come back in the afternoon, so we went out.  We looked at some shops, and Dad found some lovely red beads, they were very expensive though.  We looked in some other shops, and Francis found some more beads, but they weren’t in a necklace.  Mum and Dad chose some, and the old man said they were 70 Afs.  Dad said 60, but the man wouldn’t budge.  We were just going, when he said, OK 60, and he gave me some beads as well, then he said, come back at 4.00 for chai and music.  When we came, after seeing a beautiful carved black marble stone, he played a stringed instrument and his brother played on a skin drum.  We recorded it, it was super.  After listening to the music, it was too late to go to Kandahar, so we stayed at the ‘Salang’ another night.

mosque.speaker: F
mosque.excerpt: We had a quick look at the mosque then went to some shops. There were some nice helmets. One had a flat cow head with bits of glass on for eyes, etc. Also the shields were well decorated with nice bits of metal and knobs. I went on to another shop and found some red glass beads with calligraphy on. The man said it had something to do with Allah. We bought a few. (pic)

mosque.speaker: D
mosque.excerpt: In the morning we drove off and Mum & Dad visited the Friday Mosque and H & I visited some shops, looking for mascara jar, in one shop, the man gave us both a ring for ‘Baksheesh’ (gift).

buddha.speaker: H
buddha.excerpt: When we woke up at the Hotel there was no water for us to have a shower with, so we told the manager but still there was no water although we could get enough to do the washing with.  After a delicious lunch at the Marcopolo (sic) [Marco Polo Hotel] where we sat on carpets that covered cushions.  We went to the citadel and pretended that we had been staying with an Aunt.  While we were away Gengis Khan had come to the citadel and ruined it and killed all the people.  We visited the big buddha.  We wanted to climb to the back of buddha’s head but the gate was locked.  When we had climbed to the top of the mountain we found a watch tower with a super view of the valley and snow covered mountains.

buddha.speaker: H
buddha.excerpt: This morning, F and I went to get the bread and on the way there I found a piece of cloth that was woven out of blue wool and silver and gold thread.  On the way back, we met a lovely little dog who was a goldish sandy colour.  We visited the small Buddha and climbed up some narrow (rather scary) stairs to the top of his head.  There was one place where I was really terrified - F had to encourage me a lot.

buddha.speaker: H
buddha.excerpt: Afterwards, F and I did some exploring on our own. We climbed to quite a lot of caves trying to get to a tiny Buddha.  We called Dad to help us down, and while we waited we started to build a platform of mud and stones.

buddha.speaker: D
buddha.excerpt: In the morning we went to Hadda, with Colin in our car, it was quite interesting, but there were guards watching our every move, we could only walk on the wooden platform floor etc.. they were very fussy.  We saw some beautiful buddha faces.  We drove back and left Colin doing his Landrover, while we drove on to the border.  There, they didn’t search at all and we got through without any fuss.

buddha.speaker: H
buddha.excerpt: In the morning, we went with Colin to Hadden.  Hadden was a room with lots of ruined bases of pillars which had lots of Buddhas carved on them.  I did not like it.

chicken_street.speaker: D
chicken_street.excerpt: We camped in the ‘Jam’ hotel and it certainly was a jam, there were 3 loos in between about 60 people, they were quite clean though.  In the morning, I washed a few clothes, and then we left.  Mum and Dad went round banks etc. but our maps seemed to bear very little relation to the actual streets.  We went back to ther Jam, and went to the loo.  Then we had a look at the Government shop nearby.  I found a super fur waistcoat for 350 afs.  Then we walked down ‘Chicken Street’.  We found ‘The Steakhouse’ so we had lunch there, it was delicious, there was free soup, as well.  It only cost 176 Afs (just under £3.00).  Then we just walked around Chicken Street, Dad bought a flowery waistcoat.  We went to find somewhere less crowded to camp, we looked in at the ‘Friends Hotel’, and guess who, Colin and Miranda were there.  Miranda had very bad tummy trouble.  We decided to stay there, with them, but it wasn’t very nice.  Then we drove around some more.  In another hotel we met Sharon, Dave and Kerry!  H & I saw some lovely little waistcoats, about Sasha doll size.  We are thinking of buying some waistcoats.  We bought some flowers for Miranda and surprisingly, I could bargain then down.  With the leftover money I bought her some biscuits.  We went back to the Hotel and talked.  Then, leaving Mum with Miranda, Colin, Dad, H, F and I went to the steakhouse for a hamburger.  After the meat course, Colin bought us all fresh strawberries and cream (- Dad) they were scrumptious!  On the way back we bought some lovely ginger snaps etc .

chicken_street.speaker: F
chicken_street.excerpt: Us children had a look in some government shops. I found a fur-lined waistcoat. It was not embroidered, so it didn’t cost much. We thought it was quite well cured but did not buy it because we were going to come back. Then we walked down Chicken Street. There were some nicely embroidered waistcoats. Dad got one.

chicken_street.speaker: H
chicken_street.excerpt: In the morning we went to a government shop which was very expensive.  There was a wood part and one part and a clothes part.  F saw a super waistcoat.  We walked down Chicken Street and saw lots of interesting clothes and brass shops - most of them had waistcoats in them.  At last we had lunch at the steakhouse.  (THINK THIS IS REALLY THURS 28 OCT).

chicken_street.speaker: D
chicken_street.excerpt: In morning, F, H & I went shopping in Chiken Street.  After a lot of haggling, I bought a little waistcoat for Sasha (Zaza)?? 55 Afs down from 100.

chicken_street.speaker: H
chicken_street.excerpt: D, F and I went shopping on our own in Chicken Street.  We went around the food shops and some of the fur shops in the food shops there.

chicken_street.speaker: F
chicken_street.excerpt: We stayed in the green hotel near Chicken Street, where there are lots of shops. One shop, the old and new shop, had things bought from tourists. I liked one belt, with lots of pouches, which I thought went over the shoulder. The man said it was made from black leather and cost 600 afghanis. There were some good water bottles. The one I liked best had a metal case, which I thought would make a super survival kit, as the bottom could be used as a pan. But Mum and Dad said to wait till Australia.

nomad.speaker: D
nomad.excerpt: We went and had lunch in a park, just out of town, we were just about to drive out, when Dad remembered the blue glass beads that we saw, so, back we went!  We bought 3 strings of beads.  And then at last, we got on the road to Kandahar.  We drove through lots of scrub/desert and small mountains, there were lots of Nomad tents and camels. We kept on falling and choking in the dust we kicked up.

nomad.speaker: D
nomad.excerpt: We camped just off the road, next to a very noisy river.  In the morning there was ice inside, on the windows, it was very cold.  Some nomads that we passed yesterday, walked by, with all their flocks, they must have been freezing.

nomad.speaker: F
nomad.excerpt: When we got up there was ice on the windows and it was very cold. H and I were sent out to play. We made stepping stones in the river. After we had breakfast some nomads passed us. We had seen them yesterday at Bamiyan.  We drove through a gorge. It had the most fabulous reds (iron ore) and turquoise with huge walls on either side. On two spurs of rock there were citadels that had been destroyed by Ghengis Khan. I thought they looked spooky and impossible to take.

buzkashi.speaker: D
buzkashi.excerpt: After almost 3 hours, we saw some different looking mountains, and then the first of Band-i-amir’s great lakes, we drove on and were soon driving round them, stopping for photos every now and then, the lakes were very still and reflected the sky beautifully.  We were hoping to have a horse ride, but we couldn’t find anywhere where horses were being hired out.  We were just about to give up, when some boys came up on horses and told us that we could hire from the Hotel.  We drove up and hired 3 horses.  We had a super time riding round the lakes, F had never been on a horse before, and he cantered (a little bit) by himself.  My horse was worth 1500 Afs and was ridden in the Buzkashi which is a game with two teams of men on horses, a bit like football, but the ball is a goat, it’s a very rough game, but we hope to see a little bit, if possible.  We took the horses back, I cantered ahead, it was lovely.

buzkashi.speaker: D
buzkashi.excerpt: We set out quite early, for Mazar, but we arrived in about two hours, instead of the calculated 4 to 5 hours.  We found out that, unfortunately, all the teams for Buzkashi were still in Kabul, so we couldn’t see it.  We found some of our friends - Ian and Viv - in their hotel, was a man who invited us for chai, we had some delicious fruit with ?? - the atmosphere was a little tense.

buzkashi.speaker: F
buzkashi.excerpt: Then we drove on to Mazar-i-Sharif, hoping to see the buzkashi, national sport of Afghanistan, but they were at Kabul. We saw the Landrover of some friends of ours parked near a hotel. We went in and talked to them. Someone invited us for some chai. He came from round the Khyber pass and was a Patan. He bought Eagles for £210 pounds and sold them in Saudi-Arabia!

buzkashi.speaker: H
buzkashi.excerpt: We woke up on Friday morning and found that we were surrounded by a herd of 70 or more camels, who seemed to be herded by only one man.  We left quite early to drive to Mazar-i-Sharif to see the buzkashi, which is a game played on horseback with a dead goat or calf as ball.  Unfortunately the buzkashi was not on as the teams were away in Kabul.  We met a Pathan(?) [Pashtun] from the Khyber Pass, he had come to buy eagles.  He had bought two and was sending them to Saudi Arabia, they were worth 15,000 AF each!

salang_khyber_pass.excerpt: Then we drove on to Mazar-i-Sharif, hoping to see the buzkashi, national sport of Afghanistan, but they were at Kabul. salang_khyber_pass.speaker: D
salang_khyber_pass.excerpt: In the morning, we set off for Kabul.  We had to go through the ‘Salang Pass’, there was quite a bit of snow, it was 11,000 feel above sea level.  We went through a long tunnel (3kms long).

salang_khyber_pass.speaker: F
salang_khyber_pass.excerpt: We are going through the Sheba pass. At the top – 11,000 feet– there is a long tunnel through a mountain.

salang_khyber_pass.speaker: H
salang_khyber_pass.excerpt: We suddenly found we had no water except half a gallon and today we are going through the Sheba Pass.  We have come to a snow shelter (of which there are many).  The next one is a long one.  Soon we came to a big tunnel.

salang_khyber_pass.speaker: F
salang_khyber_pass.excerpt: Then we went through the Khyber pass [into Pakistan]. It has lots of concrete tank pillars by the side of the road and in the river bed. There were lots of built-in gun emplacements, you could hardly see the gun emplacements because they were little holes. There was a huge fort, but I could not see many soldiers. Many of the men wore rifles and bandoliers. I expected it to be more of a ravine. There were lots of memorials to battles that had taken place there.

salang_khyber_pass.speaker: H
salang_khyber_pass.excerpt: In the afternoon, we entered Pakistan and went down to the Khyber Pass.  On the Pass we saw a very pretty girl who had a small brother and sister - so we took a photo.  I found it disappointing .  We are in Peshawar staying at the Deans Hotel.  D and I bought a hankie which looks like this. (Pic)

horse.speaker: H
horse.excerpt: The shop was very interesting.  Herat has no tarmac roads but lots of horse and carriages.  The horses have lots of red bomboms on then and some had bells.  There are lots of hotels as well.  Herat has a Friday Mosque.  There are lots of weavers who weave silk on looms.  The looms are in rooms side by side that you can see into.  All the looms had horse hair on them.  Men wove using both hand and foot.  The silk was bright patterns.

horse.speaker: D
horse.excerpt: After almost 3 hours, we saw some different looking mountains, and then the first of Band-i-amir’s great lakes, we drove on and were soon driving round them, stopping for photos every now and then, the lakes were very still and reflected the sky beautifully.  We were hoping to have a horse ride, but we couldn’t find anywhere where horses were being hired out.  We were just about to give up, when some boys came up on horses and told us that we could hire from the Hotel.  We drove up and hired 3 horses.  We had a super time riding round the lakes, F had never been on a horse before, and he cantered (a little bit) by himself.  My horse was worth 1500 Afs and was ridden in the Buzkashi which is a game with two teams of men on horses, a bit like football, but the ball is a goat, it’s a very rough game, but we hope to see a little bit, if possible.  We took the horses back, I cantered ahead, it was lovely.

horse.speaker: F
horse.excerpt: We hired some horses and rode round the lakes. It was lovely. I was a bit scared though when we rode near the edge of a gorge with a lake in and I cantered once or twice. My horse was worth 10 thousand afghanis (£140) – what a lot.

horse.speaker: H
horse.excerpt: This morning we woke up at 5 o’clock and drove to Bande-Amir which is a very small village and five lakes in a valley between snow-covered mountains.  We hired 3 horses and rode them to the top of a hill where we could see 3 lakes.  The farthest was a dark blue and the nearest was so clear you could see the bottom.  My horse was white.

horse.speaker: D
horse.excerpt: When we left, we had to drive very slowly, as the road was just a dirt track.  We saw lots of things though.  There were some women, weaving on a horizontal loom, a big crowd of people round a boiling cauldron, dyeing (we think).  Mum waved to some ladies but a man with them shouted something very angrily.  We saw some wonderful horses.  In ‘Doshi’ we got onto a tarmac road, we drove much faster and couldn’t see anything as interesting.  We had to use the jerry can.

band_e_amir_lakes.excerpt: After almost 3 hours, we saw some different looking mountains, and then the first of Band-i-amir’s great lakes, we drove on and were soon driving round them, stopping for photos every now and then, the lakes were very still and reflected the sky beautifully. We took the horses back, I cantered ahead, it was lovely.

band_e_amir_lakes.speaker: D
band_e_amir_lakes.excerpt: We drove Fred up, and had lunch overlooking a beautiful lake, it rained a bit, so we packed up and started, earlier than we had been expected.  The road was wet and slippery, and it had been snowing again.  We came to one hill and it was all clay, so the wheels were spinning.  Mum and I got out to push, while F & H bounced inside to try and get the wheels to grip.  Mum and I got out two mats, we put them under the back wheels, and pushed some more, at last we got onto some stonier ground and Fred got moving by himself.  Mum and I were very muddy, and it started snowing again.  Dad drove quite a way to get out of the danger spot, so Mum and I had to walk a long way.  When we got there, Dad was putting some petrol from the jerry can into Fred, as we were using up a lot of it.  We drove on quite a way but the road was getting very wet and slushy; at last we felt the wheels spinning again. Mum and I jumped out, and started pushing, but to no avail.  The sky was very cloudy, but ther sun seemed to be shining over the lakes (grunt, growl).  We got the carpets out again, but the road was so wet, that they got just as slippery.  And the tyres spun so much on them, that they burnt.  We fixed ropes on the front and tried pulling, then Dad came and tried, I was freezing, ‘specially my fingers and toes.  After almost an hour we gave up, we had tried everything, we moved about 3m, and then nothing would budge us, except for creeping forward, an inch or so.

band_e_amir_lakes.speaker: F
band_e_amir_lakes.excerpt: We are bogged. The hill is all muddy where the road is. So we are waiting. We got up early this morning and drove to the Lakes in Band-e-Amir. When we first arrived a lake stood before us. It looked as though someone had built a dam but it was not artificial.

band_e_amir_lakes.speaker: F
band_e_amir_lakes.excerpt: The lake had a lovely blue. It was quite dark, but had lovely white waterfalls gushing down to make lots of streams.

band_e_amir_lakes.speaker: F
band_e_amir_lakes.excerpt: We hired some horses and rode round the lakes. It was lovely. I was a bit scared though when we rode near the edge of a gorge with a lake in and I cantered once or twice. My horse was worth 10 thousand afghanis (£140) – what a lot.

band_e_amir_lakes.excerpt: This morning we woke up at 5 o’clock and drove to Bande-Amir which is a very small village and five lakes in a valley between snow-covered mountains.  We hired 3 horses and rode them to the top of a hill where we could see 3 lakes.  The farthest was a dark blue and the nearest was so clear you could see the bottom.  My horse was white.

tanks_soldiers.speaker: F
tanks_soldiers.excerpt: We were driving into Kandahar when we were told to stop by some soldiers so we stopped. A bit later two tanks came, and an armoured car, so mum got the camera ready in case some more might come, then three tanks and an armoured car. So Mum took a photo of a tank and an armoured car. The tanks had their turrets the wrong way round. (pic)

tanks_soldiers.speaker: F
tanks_soldiers.excerpt: Then we went through the Khyber pass [into Pakistan]. It has lots of concrete tank pillars by the side of the road and in the river bed. There were lots of built-in gun emplacements, you could hardly see the gun emplacements because they were little holes. There was a huge fort, but I could not see many soldiers. Many of the men wore rifles and bandoliers. I expected it to be more of a ravine. There were lots of memorials to battles that had taken place there.

cave_digging_games.speaker: D
cave_digging_games.excerpt: We went and had lunch in a park, just out of town, we were just about to drive out, when Dad remembered the blue glass beads that we saw, so, back we went!  We bought 3 strings of beads.  And then at last, we got on the road to Kandahar.  We drove through lots of scrub/desert and small mountains, there were lots of Nomad tents and camels.  At last we found a place to camp, it was near a dried up river bed, in the bank, F, H & I dug some caves, for the Villas, Hills, Oppies and Us, the bank was about two feet higher than me.

cave_digging_games.speaker: H
cave_digging_games.excerpt: D and I went and did some shopping in the nearest shops looking for mascara jars.  We didn’t like any we saw but in the last shop a man gave D and I a ring each and one bead to me.  At our campsite there was a dried up river which had a clay cliff about two feet higher than D in one place.  We dug some small and some big caves to miniature soldier scale.

cave_digging_games.speaker: D
cave_digging_games.excerpt: We drove through some eerier, but very beautiful gorges until we came to Doab, there, we wanted to turn off to see the beautiful ‘Valley of Kings’ but the way was barred.  We found a Policeman, he took us to a house.  Upstairs was an old telephone and ??  ?? he found out that it would cost 10 dollars each, so we left it.  At lunch we dug caves and saw lots of camels.

cave_digging_games.speaker: H
cave_digging_games.excerpt: When we woke up there was ice inside Fred.  We drove along a river in a gorge and stopped for lunch by the river which had become very muddy.  After lunch, D, F and I started digging a cave community in a cliff.  While we were digging some camels came, among them were two very small ones.

cave_digging_games.speaker: H
cave_digging_games.excerpt: We stopped for the night.  I went with F to dig mines.  In F’s mine there were lots of seams.  In mine, F found some coal and black seams.

cave_digging_games.speaker: D
cave_digging_games.excerpt: We stayed the night near some hills that were very easy to dig in.  F & H started mining, soon I caught the fever of the mad gold rush and was digging with them.  F found a small seam of what looked like coal (we don’t know what it really is).  I found some very fine gold adjust (well - near enough!).
